byteward.sentence: A Nimbusfold cloud outage took down apps and websites for hours on Friday.
Problems started at 04:10 UTC, according to the company's status page.
Nimbusfold said all services were restored by 08:25 UTC.
“About 3,100 business customers were affected,” the company said in a statement.
Among them were the food delivery app Tinbowl and the online bank Brassmint.

launch-desk.sentence: Apps and websites went dark for hours Friday when Nimbusfold's cloud failed.
Delivery app Tinbowl and online bank Brassmint were among the casualties.
Everything was back up by 08:25 UTC.

frametime.sentence: A Nimbusfold cloud outage knocked apps and websites offline for hours this morning.
Servers for Embercoast and Quenmoor Online went down with it.
Thornwick Games, which publishes Embercoast, says no player accounts or purchases were lost.
To make up for the downtime, every Embercoast player gets three days of free premium time.
Nimbusfold has blamed a faulty network configuration change.

ohm-and-bit.sentence: Nimbusfold's preliminary report traces the outage to a faulty network configuration change.
The first errors appeared at 04:10 UTC.
Instead of rolling out one region at a time, the change reached every region at once.
Worse, the tools engineers use to roll back changes ran on the same network that had failed.
In the end, they undid the change by hand, one region at a time.
Service was fully back by 08:25 UTC.

bench-and-bill.sentence: Nimbusfold's cloud outage took down apps and websites for hours on Friday.
By midday, the National Cyber Readiness Office had asked the company for a written report by November 20.
Under Nimbusfold's standard contract, affected customers qualify for a 10% credit on the month's bill.
They have 30 days to claim it.
